title: The Tip That Reads a Difference

scenes.visual: Title card: The Tip That Reads a Difference.

scenes.tts: How does the tip of a growing axon know which way to turn?
scenes.visual: A nerve cell on a dark dish; its axon ends in a flat fan. Title card: The tip that reads a difference.
scenes.narration: How does the tip of a growing axon know which way to turn?

scenes.tts: An axon is the long fibre a nerve cell sends out to reach its partner.
scenes.visual: The axon extends across the dish toward a distant partner cell.
scenes.narration: An axon is the long fibre a nerve cell sends out to reach its partner.

scenes.tts: At its end is a flat, moving fan called the growth cone.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into the fan at the axon tip. Label: growth cone.
scenes.narration: At its end is a flat, moving fan called the growth cone.

scenes.tts: Microtubules fill the centre of the fan. Actin fills its edge, in thin spikes and flat sheets.
scenes.visual: Top-down growth cone: green microtubules in the central domain, red actin in the periphery. Labels: central domain, peripheral domain.
scenes.narration: Microtubules fill the centre of the fan. Actin fills its edge, in thin spikes and flat sheets.

scenes.tts: The spikes are filopodia. They are feelers and feet at once, sampling the ground and gripping it.
scenes.visual: Filopodia flick out, touch the surface and attach. Labels: filopodia, lamellipodia.
scenes.narration: The spikes are filopodia. They are feelers and feet at once, sampling the ground and gripping it.

scenes.tts: Molecules outside the cell, called guidance cues, attract or repel the growth cone.
scenes.visual: Small cue molecules drift near the fan; some pull, some push. Label: guidance cues.
scenes.narration: Molecules outside the cell, called guidance cues, attract or repel the growth cone.

scenes.tts: In a classic test, a fine pipette releases a cue beside a living growth cone.
scenes.visual: A glass pipette tip sits beside the growth cone; a soft cue cloud spreads from it.
scenes.narration: In a classic test, a fine pipette releases a cue beside a living growth cone.

scenes.tts: The cue thins with distance. So the near side meets a little more than the far side.
scenes.visual: The cloud is shaded slightly darker on the near edge of the fan than on the far edge.
scenes.narration: The cue thins with distance. So the near side meets a little more than the far side.

scenes.tts: How much more? In the standard assay, only about five to ten percent.
scenes.visual: On screen: near side about 5 to 10% more than far side (standard assay). Ruler: cone about 10 micrometres wide in these assays, pipette about 100 micrometres away.
scenes.narration: How much more? In the standard assay, only about five to ten percent.

scenes.tts: Now flood the whole dish with ten times more cue. Do growth cones turn harder?
scenes.visual: The whole dish fills evenly with dense cue. Question mark over several growth cones.
scenes.narration: Now flood the whole dish with ten times more cue. Do growth cones turn harder?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: No. Across many cones there is no net turn. There is more cue, but no difference between the sides.
scenes.visual: Many growth cones wander; their tracks scatter evenly around the starting heading. Both edges shaded the same. Label: no difference, no preferred direction.
scenes.narration: No. Across many cones there is no net turn. There is more cue, but no difference between the sides.

scenes.visual: Side-by-side: gradient (tracks bias toward the source) and uniform bath (tracks scatter around zero).

scenes.tts: So the difference across the width gives the direction. The overall amount changes how strongly cones respond.
scenes.visual: Caption card: the difference gives the direction; the overall amount changes the response.
scenes.narration: So the difference across the width gives the direction. The overall amount changes how strongly cones respond.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule, for a growth cone on a flat surface in a dish. The edge moves forward by the actin added there, minus the actin that slides back.
scenes.visual: Edge close-up: red actin added at the front, streaming back. On screen: advance = added − slides back. Label: simplified culture model.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule, for a growth cone on a flat surface in a dish. The edge moves forward by the actin added there, minus the actin that slides back.

scenes.tts: Grip on the ground, the clutch, holds back part of that slide.
scenes.visual: Adhesion molecules under the fan grab the surface; a clutch icon engages; the backward streaming slows above the grip.
scenes.narration: Grip on the ground, the clutch, holds back part of that slide.

scenes.tts: A turn sticks where microtubules move in and build new axon. Microtubules can also start the turn themselves.
scenes.visual: The near side bulges; green microtubules enter it; the fan narrows behind into new shaft. Inset: actin and microtubules remodel together. Label: simplified culture model.
scenes.narration: A turn sticks where microtubules move in and build new axon. Microtubules can also start the turn themselves.

scenes.tts: Three questions follow. How can a tip move forward while much of its actin streams backward?
scenes.visual: Question card 1: actin slides back, so how does the edge advance?
scenes.narration: Three questions follow. How can a tip move forward while much of its actin streams backward?

scenes.tts: How does so small a difference become a turn of the whole axon?
scenes.visual: Question card 2: a 5 to 10% difference, a whole turn?
scenes.narration: How does so small a difference become a turn of the whole axon?

scenes.tts: And can the tip make that decision on its own?
scenes.visual: Question card 3: can the tip decide alone?
scenes.narration: And can the tip make that decision on its own?

scenes.tts: Carry one idea. A cue gives a direction by making the two sides of the growth cone differ.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a cue gives a direction by making the two sides differ.
scenes.narration: Carry one idea. A cue gives a direction by making the two sides of the growth cone differ.

scenes.visual: End card.
